__comment: Curated acquisition manifest for scripts/acquire-art.mjs (phase V4). One entry per plate, each a deliberate choice with its reason recorded — no crawling, no category sweeps. The licence is NOT stated here: acquire-art.mjs reads it from the Commons API at acquisition and refuses anything it cannot prove is public domain or CC0. A title in this file is a proposal, not a permission.

acquisitions.title: File:Gustave Doré - Dante Alighieri - Inferno - Plate 9 (Canto III - Charon).jpg
acquisitions.why: A ferryman poling a crowded boat across black water under a low sky. The region is a crossing, and the plate is about the toll for one — the chart's nodes read as landings.

acquisitions.title: File:Gustave Doré - Dante Alighieri - Inferno - Plate 65 (Canto XXXI - The Titans).jpg
acquisitions.why: A shaft walled by vast half-seen figures, light falling from far above. Reads as depth rather than as a cave mouth, which is what the caverns map actually is.

acquisitions.title: File:Gustave Doré - Ludgate Hill.jpg
acquisitions.why: Doré's London: A Pilgrimage (1872). A choked street under a railway bridge, all soot and traffic. A city that is grim by ordinary congestion, not by monsters — the register the house wants.

acquisitions.title: File:Gustave Doré - Wentworth Street Whitechapel - London, a Pilgrimage.jpg
acquisitions.why: A packed slum street from the same series. Domestic, crowded, poor — the right backdrop for a village chart, and it pairs with Ludgate Hill so the two settled regions share a hand.

acquisitions.title: File:Bpt6k10470488 f369.jpg
acquisitions.why: "Off Billingsgate" (Doré, London: A Pilgrimage, 1872) — fishermen on the rigging of a moored boat, a forest of masts against a backlit sky. The vertical mast lines and lit sky band read as a dramatic ground for a composited foe, the way the ruined-city plate's skyline does; the coastal village's first arena, per the V4/V5 follow-up.

acquisitions.title: File:Rorschach_blot_01.jpg
acquisitions.why: Real ink on paper, not a drawn approximation of ink — the honest source for a splatter motif. Plate I, the test's own opener, symmetric and dense enough to read at 48px.

acquisitions.title: File:Rorschach_blot_03.jpg
acquisitions.why: Plate III's figure has a looser, more scattered silhouette than plate I — the variety `<Splatter seed>` picks between, same family of source so the set reads as one kit.

acquisitions.title: File:Rorschach_blot_04.jpg
acquisitions.why: Plate IV, dense and clawed at the edges — the heaviest-looking blot of the set, good for the larger renders (combat victory panel, map canvas).

acquisitions.title: File:Rorschach_blot_06.jpg
acquisitions.why: Plate VI's long drip trail at the base reads as spatter rather than a blob, rounding out the set with the one shape that actually looks flung rather than pooled.

acquisitions.title: File:YCBA London a Pilgrimage 07.jpg
acquisitions.region: fallback (every region with no rule of its own)
acquisitions.why: "The New Zealander" (Dore, London: A Pilgrimage, 1873) - a cloaked figure sits on a broken wharf sketching the ruins of a dead city across black water under a clouded moon. It replaces `arena-ruined-city.jpg`, which was saturated pixel art of modern high-rises among nine wood engravings AND carried licence UNRESOLVED. The fallback is the most-seen arena in the game, so it needs the most neutral composition in the set: heavy dark mass at the edges and along the bottom, a lit sky band and a ruined skyline across the middle where the foe composites, and nothing so place-specific that it contradicts an unrelated region. The source is a page scan, hence the plate-page recipe.

acquisitions.title: File:Gottliche Komodie. T. 2, Das Fegefeuer 1871 (148974123).jpg
acquisitions.region: launcher icon (the title plate until plan 121.2)
acquisitions.why: Purgatorio, Canto I: Dante and Virgil meet Cato on an empty shore before dawn, under a wide low sky. Chosen by T (2026-10-11) as serene but unsettling and not busy; the open sky carries the wordmark, and Purgatorio is the canticle of penance, as the psalm is.
acquisitions.darkRatioWhy: the dawn sky (luminance ~145) is lighter than the default cut-off (0.82 x mean), so the detector dropped it; 0.95 finds the printed border at 17.4% of the page height, measured 17.8%

acquisitions.title: File:Gustave Doré - Dante Alighieri - Inferno - Plate 3 (The lion).jpg
acquisitions.why: Inferno, Canto I: Dante alone in the dark wood, the lion on the rock before him, one pale slit of sky between the cliffs. Picked by T (2026-11-03): "It's got a huge area at the top we could put the title in". The dark upper band carries the wordmark; the slit sits under it. The launcher icon stays on shore-at-dawn.
